analysis: Integration review of a rollback-switch forwarding change. Production change: LaunchAgent.swift adds SSDPrefixCachePolicy.incrementalCheckpointsFlag (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS) to LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys (patch hunk near head line 372) with a doc comment (~line 332). A test in LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (head ~336-359) asserts the key is on the provider allowlist, not the WatchdogAgent allowlist, that unrelated secrets stay excluded, and that foreground and launchd resolve identical modes. The remaining files (changelog, cli-reference.md line 1960, configuration.md line 685, ssd-kv-cache.md lines 3 and 311-316) are documentation that matches the code change. Across the batch analyses, the units are consistent: the change only forwards an operator-set, disable-only boolean into the launchd plist. The operator is already inside TB-003/ADV-001 and can already set DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 and other allowlisted keys. The knob selects delta versus complete checkpoint writes and does not touch the DBK3 AES-GCM, KEK-rooted HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping, 30-minute TTL, disk budget or KEK purge that T-041 relies on. Test-root and persistent-key benchmark controls remain off the allowlist, and the test pins this for unrelated secrets. No finding qualifies. Residual uncertainty: the delta-checkpoint write/read implementation (SSDPrefixCachePolicy, SSDBlockStore, SSDPrefixCache) is not in this diff. Whether delta files keep HMAC-only names, AAD binding, salt/model/weightHash scoping, TTL purge of dependent chains and fail-closed behavior on a missing parent is a pre-existing or other-PR question. T-041's text does not mention delta checkpoints, so a threat-model note may be warranted. Note that 32 source units were omitted from replay.
